evidence.claim: Hubbell Power Systems lists utility product categories including bushings, power apparatus bushings, small apparatus bushings, arresters, insulators, connectors, switching and fusing equipment.

A Hubbell Power Systems substation brochure describes PCORE as a North American bushing provider focused on porcelain oil-filled capacitance-graded bushings and related components for transformers and oil circuit breakers.

Cleveland-Cliffs states that it offers grain-oriented and non-oriented electrical steels for transformers, generators, and motors and calls itself the only producer of electrical steels in North America.

Cleveland-Cliffs' Zanesville Works page says regular grain-oriented electrical steels are used for power and distribution transformers and that the site serves power and distribution transformer markets.
Worthington Steel describes itself as a public NYSE-listed metals processor with capabilities including carbon flat-rolled steel processing and electrical steel laminations.
Worthington Steel may have transformer-core exposure if its electrical steel laminations are used by transformer OEMs; this specific end-market mapping was not proven in the gathered evidence.
Preformed Line Products annual-report search evidence describes the company as supplying formed wire products and related hardware used in energy and utility networks.

External search context framed PLPC as a niche transmission-hardware company whose order intake may precede line construction, but this is adjacent to transformer components rather than direct exposure.

memory_update.text: HUBB is the clearest US-listed reference candidate for transformer bushings and adjacent utility apparatus components; direct but already better known.
CLF should be tracked as a transformer-core upstream materials candidate because GOES supply can become a pacing item for transformer production.
WS is an underfollowed hypothesis: electrical steel laminations may map to transformer-core processing, but end-market and customer exposure must be verified before promotion.
PLPC is an adjacent speculative-shadow candidate for transmission hardware, not a direct transformer-component supplier; keep only if the funnel expands to line/substation hardware bottlenecks.

US-listed pure-play CTC magnet-wire, tap-changer, insulation-paper, and transformer-core component suppliers were not clearly identified in this pass; many likely remain private, foreign-listed, or embedded inside diversified industrials.

node: Transformer component supply chain: CTC magnet wire, cores, insulation, bushings, tap changers, and specialized subcomponents
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a small US-listed universe with plausible transformer-component or adjacent grid-hardware exposure. The cleanest direct public-market mappings are Hubbell for bushings/arresters/insulators and Cleveland-Cliffs for grain-oriented electrical steel used in transformer cores. Worthington Steel is a lower-attention candidate via electrical steel laminations and processing, but its exact transformer-core revenue exposure needs verification. Preformed Line Products is not a transformer-component supplier, but is included as an underfollowed adjacent transmission-hardware beneficiary that may surface when transformer bottlenecks migrate into broader substation and line-build procurement.
